sections.heading: Halaman 37: Glossary
sections.content:
36 | P a g e 
www.irispower.com 
7 GLOSSARY 
Term Definition 
Ageing The development of failure mechanisms 
Asphalt Thermoplastic binder to consolidate insulating tape layers 
Amplification An increase in magnitude 
Attenuation A reduction in magnitude 
Bar (half coil) Coils made in half-sections for easier installation in long core or small diameter bore 
machines - one turn per coil 
Bottom bar The bar further from the stator core bore 
Breakdown voltage The voltage at which a pulse spark will occur across a void 
Capacitance Is the electrical property that stores an electrical charge by impeding a change in 
voltage 
Capacitive couplers PD sensors that block the 50/60Hz signal and pass the high-frequency PD signals 
(80pf capacitors) 
Capacitive coupling Travel of a high-frequency signal due to the capacitance property of materials 
Phase-to-ground PD 
pulses 
Pulses that occur within the slot portion of the coil and are phase-to-ground voltage 
dependent - negative clumps near 45 and positive near 225 on the 3-D plot 
Contamination The presence of any conductive or partially conductive material in the endwinding 
area 
Corona Visible surface partial discharges that occur when the gas adjacent to an exposed 
conductor ionizes 
Cross-coupled PD activity PD that occurs on another phase from the one that detects it 
De-bond The loss of mechanical strength of a resin which bonds layers of insulting tape 
together; also called delamination 
Delay time In a directional (BUS) install, the time in nanoseconds it takes for a high frequency 
pulse to travel from one coupler to the other 
Differential (PDA) A style of sensor installation that uses simultaneous pulse arrival for disturbance 
separation 
Direct (Positive) effect When an increase in the operating or ambient condition causes an increase in PD 
– can be attributed to load, temperature, hydrogen pressure or ambient humidity 
Directional (BUS) A style of sensor installation that uses arrival time for disturbance separation 
Dispersion An increase in rise-time due to high frequency pulse traveling waveforms 
Electrical breakdown The theoretical V/mm stress of a gas medium that if exceeded will result in an arc - 
for air it is EBD = 3kV (peak)/mm at STP 
Electrical slot discharge Surface PD that occurs within the slot portion of the coil due to inadequate semi-
conductive coating 
Electrical tracking The current that flows when a conductive path of surface contamination occurs 
between two coils at different potentials - frequently across coil blocking

sections.heading: Halaman 38: Glossary
sections.content:
37 | P a g e 
www.irispower.com 
Endwinding (end arm) That portion of the coil or bar that extends beyond the stator core 
Endwinding discharges Discharges that occur in the end arm area typically between high voltage coils or 
bars of different phases 
Endwinding vibration 100/120Hz or rotational speed frequency vibration of the endwinding due to 
mechanical stresses 
Epoxy Organic resin used to bond tape layers - usually thermoset 
Excitation pulses 
Pulses that look like PD, but are really from the thyristor firing of the excitation 
system – typically low magnitudes and occur at uniform phase locations across the 
cycle, usually six. 
Form-wound coils Coils designed such that the turn voltage stress is constant at power system 
frequency which is normally 50 or 60 Hz 
Frequency - pulse The inverse of four times the rise-time (f = 1 / 4 * rise-time) 
Girth cracking A crack around the circumference of the coil at slot exit - normally caused by 
Thermal Cycling of asphaltic insulation systems 
Glass Fibreglass materials used in insulation systems - these may be glass fibre (roving), 
glass tape or glass felt materials 
Global VPI When the VPI process is applied to an entire stator after the green coils or bars 
have been secured inside the stator core 
Glow discharge A type of partial discharge phenomenon characterized by a diffused glow [1] 
Grading coating (stress 
control coating) 
A silicon-carbide tape or paint that is applied to the outside portion of the coil/bar 
starting beyond the slot exit and extending into the endwinding - used for voltage 
stress control – extent of surface covered is voltage dependent 
Green coil A dry-tape coil which has not yet been subjected to a VPI process or a resin rich 
coil which has not been pressed and cured 
Groundwall insulation The layers of insulation that are wrapped around the entire coil side or bar to 
withstand the voltage to ground electric stress 
Guard system Continuous monitoring systems for monitoring PD activity in generators and motors 
– HydroGuard, BusGuard and TurboGuard 
GuardII system 
Second generation continuous monitoring systems for monitoring PD activity in 
generators and motors, expandable for other monitoring technologies such as rotor 
flux and endwinding vibration 
Humidity effect When there is a substantial change in PD with a change in humidity -- this is most 
often an indication of surface contamination 
Hydrogen pressure effect When there is a substantial change in PD with a change in hydrogen pressure -- a 
normal phenomenon, but more apparent with surface PD activity 
Impedance The electrical property that opposes the flow of current 
Impedance mismatch The natural tendency of high-frequency pulses to attenuate or amplify when they 
traverse from a material of one characteristic impedance level to another 
Impregnation The manufacturing process that forces resin to seep and cure between the layers 
of tape

sections.heading: Halaman 39: Glossary
sections.content:
38 | P a g e 
www.irispower.com 
Improper impregnation When a coil or bar is not properly impregnated with organic resin during 
manufacturing and has voids within the insulation structure 
Internal delamination The de-bonding of tape layers due to thermal stresses 
Inductance The electrical property that produces an electromagnetic field by impeding a 
change of the current 
Insulation failure A complete electrical discharge that occurs between two metallic electrodes 
Inverse (Negative) effect When an increase in the operating or ambient condition causes a decrease in PD – 
can be attributed to load, temperature, hydrogen pressure or ambient humidity 
Ladder-effect 
Result of coil vibration where the portion of the coil adjacent to the core abrades 
and that near the ventilation ducts does not - the pattern of the damage outside the 
coil resembles a ladder 
Line-end coil The coil connected to the circuit ring or phase bus - will have maximum phase-to-
ground voltage 
Load cycling Frequent changes in the machine’s load current due to either real and reactive 
power 
Load effect When there is a substantial change in PD with a change in load -- if positive 
predominant as well, this is an indication of loose coils 
Loose coils Coils that are inadequately secured within the slot and thus vibrate due to the 
mechanical and magnetic stresses in a machine 
Mica The principal insulating dielectric material of stator windings - it is a durable but 
brittle mineral product 
Multi-turn coil Coils made with several conductor turns 
Negative predominance 
When the amount of negative phase-to-ground PD, near 45°, is higher than the 
amount of positive phase-to-ground PD near 225° -- indicative of slot insulation 
voids near the conductors 
No load test Test at no load or reduced load for determining load effect by comparing results to 
a full load test 
No polarity predominance 
When the amount of negative classic PD, near 45, is approximately equal to the 
amount of positive classic PD, near 225 -- indicative of voids within the slot 
insulation bulk 
Noise Pulses originating from outside of the insulation system, or pulses that do not 
exhibit PD characteristics 
Disturbance separation The technique used to ensure that only machine PD is detected and not PD-like 
disturbances from sources outside the machine stator winding 
Disturbance-like PD 
Non-classic PD detected by the machine coupler, which consists of small 
magnitude pulses occurring across the AC cycle. This is usually not indicative of a 
problem, and as the winding ages “true” PD will eventually be observed beyond the 
disturbance-like PD. 
NQN Normalized Quantity Number - represents the area beneath the curve of the 2-D 
plots weighted by the magnitude of the pulses

sections.heading: Halaman 40: Glossary
sections.content:
39 | P a g e 
www.irispower.com 
Organic bonding material Made of organic substance used to bond insulating tape layers - asphalt, polyester, 
and epoxy 
Over voltage When the voltage stress across a void exceeds the breakdown voltage 
Ozone O3 - a by-product of electrical discharges in air, aggressive oxidizer 
Partial discharge An incomplete, or partial, electrical discharge that occurs between insulation and 
either insulation or a metallic electrode 
PDA-IV Partial Discharge Analyzer - test instrument for monitoring PD activity in hydro 
generators 
Phase-to-Phase 
Discharge 
PD that is phase-to-phase voltage dependent and originates outside of the slot 
from contamination, electrical tracking, or inadequate spacing – pulses clump 30° 
phase-shifted from the phase-to-ground PD positions (or 15°, 75°, 195°, and 255°) 
with corresponding opposite polarity pulse patterns in the two phases between 
which PD is occurring 
Polarity predominance When the Qm of one polarity is greater than that of the other polarity, or there is a 
separation of the two lines on the 2-D plot 
Polyester Organic resin used to bond tape layers - usually a thermoset material 
Positive predominance 
When the amount of positive phase-to-ground PD, around 225°, is higher than the 
amount of negative phase-to-ground PD, near 45° -- usually indicative of surface 
activity 
Pseudo-glow discharge A type of partial discharge characterized by current pulses of relatively small 
amplitude, and generally, a long rise time 
Qm Peak PD magnitude in mV measured at a repetition rate of 10 pulses per second 
Radiation Energy emitted from a central point in the form of waves or particles 
Resin-loaded tapes Tapes that are epoxy-loaded and are directly applied to the bars - they are cured 
with heat and pressure 
Rise-time The time required for a pulse to increase from 10% to 90% of its peak magnitude 
RTD Resistive temperature detector - used for monitoring stator winding temperatures 
Semi-conducting slot 
coating 
A carbon-loaded tape or paint that is applied to the outside of the portion of the coil 
or bar that will be in contact with the core - used for voltage stress control for 
voltage ratings of 6 kV and above and for motors with lower voltage ratings if fed 
from a variable voltage and frequency converter 
Side packing 
The material used to fill up the space between a coil or bar side and the stator core 
- can be rigid or conformable, and is usually semi-conductive for voltage ratings of 
6 kV and above and for motors with lower voltage ratings if fed from a variable 
voltage and frequency converter 
Signal-to-noise ratio 
(SNR) 
The logarithmic ratio of the PD signal to noise. A high SNR is necessary for noise 
separation. 
Slot discharges Discharges that occur on a random basis involving a large surface of coil or bar, 
separated from the grounded core by an air gap – positive predominance 
Slot portion The portion of the coil/bar located within the stator core section

sections.heading: Halaman 41: Glossary
sections.content:
40 | P a g e 
www.irispower.com 
Stator slot couplers (SSC) Wideband antenna installed beneath the wedges or between the bars, which is 
capable of distinguishing PD based on pulse characteristics 
Temperature effect When a change in temperature affects the PD levels 
TGA Turbine Generator Analyzer - test instrument for monitoring PD activity in turbine 
generators and motors 
Thermoplastic A coil insulating system the binding materials of which become somewhat soft and 
pliable with an increase in temperature – asphaltic-mica is a classic example 
Thermoset A coil insulating system the binding materials of which set up rigidly and are 
relatively unaffected by normal operating temperatures – epoxy-mica is an example 
Time-of-arrival A disturbance separation technique that compares the arrival of pulses at two 
different couplers to determine the direction of the PD source 
Top bar The bar closest to the armature 
Trac monitor Continuous monitoring systems for monitoring PD activity in generators and motors 
– HydroTrac, BusTrac and PDTrac 
BusTracII, HydroTracII 
and PDTracII monitor 
Second generation continuous monitoring systems for monitoring PD activity in 
generators and motors 
Transmission Travel of an electrical current through a conductor 
Turn insulation A dedicated layer of insulation surrounding each turn in a multi-turn coil 
Vacuum pressure 
impregnation (VPI) 
An impregnation process that involves creating a vacuum, injecting resin, and 
applying pressure - can be done on a batch of coils or the entire stator 
Voltage stress control The application of semi-conductive and grading materials to control electrical 
stresses on the surface of coil insulation
